title: The Network Takes a Cut
audience: Short-video audience, phones first; a 30-second paper-cut explainer of how Uber earns money
notes: The user's brief: explain how Uber makes money. The facts are public and deliberately general: Uber is asset-light (it does not own the cars, kitchens or freight it moves); riders pay a fare; the driver keeps the fare minus a service fee; Uber also earns from delivery, freight, advertising and memberships (Uber One); the network effect makes waits shorter as more riders and drivers join. No exact take rate, revenue number, city, date or person is invented. The two performers are role characters: Rider (the star) and Driver (the foil). They are not new personal names; the film invents no person, city, date, logo, revenue number or take rate. The film is 30 s, five beats, ten shots, no logo and no brand mark: the word 'Uber' appears only as the subject of the explainer.
